scores.why: All seven modules have backend endpoints and screens: matchmaking with personal-data masking, voice input and LLM explanations; library, county map and learning materials; idea card, canvas and grant draft; usability tester; Q&A and mentor booking; admin with trend radar; municipality adapter with cost estimate. Held back because matchmaking is keyword-based over only 10 seeded innovations.

Docker Compose, documented API, open data API with webhooks, a monthly cost estimate (170–200 zł), 49 tests and a live deploy. Limits: SQLite, per-innovation costs hand-written, default admin password.

Two contrast modes, larger text, plain-language mode always on, page reader, legible typeface, skip link, focus trap, accessibility statement; documented axe audit from 82 violations to 0 across 18 pages × 6 settings.
Clean, credible public-sector UI, an original hex map, an idea poster, a 10-slide deck and extensive docs. Visually conservative and dense; no video in the repo.

projects.live_demo: malopolski-hub-2026.vercel.app responds with the LLM configured (not linked in README)
projects.built_during_event: partly: first commit was 12k lines about 2h20m after the start, then 67 commits until Sunday 08:14 CEST
strengths: Accessibility measured with before/after audit numbers
Explainable matchmaking with personal data masked before the LLM
Works without an LLM key, one-command start, 49 tests, live deploy
Clear running-cost estimate and GDPR notes
weaknesses: Only 10 demo innovations; keyword matchmaking, not semantic
No video in the repo; demo URL not in README
red_flags: 12k-line first commit two hours in suggests heavy AI generation or pre-event preparation
Deck claims full WCAG 2.1 AA from a self-audit only
projects.verdict: The most complete and accessible HubMI entry reviewed; every module works, held back by shallow matchmaking over a tiny catalogue.

excluded.reason: Not a HubMI entry: the team's own context file says SiteQuest was built for the Smart City task after they dropped a HubMI plan on 3 Oct. It has no matchmaking or ROPS modules, so it is probably not the HubMI finalist 'SideQuest' entry.

calibration_note: MHIS is clearly strong because every module exists in code with tests, a live deploy and audited accessibility.
